trigger_context: Tell me about the mound network as a distributed capacitor array and the star fort geometry on the silicon substrate at Cahokia.
raw_content:
The corpus has an entry for exactly this claim, and the entry's purpose is to refuse it. [E-W0-010-01] is titled "Star Fort / Mound grid operational on silicon substrate" and its body is a retraction: the framings of the mound network as a "distributed capacitor array," the attribution of "star fort geometry," and the "fractal antenna patterns on a silicon substrate" all have no scholarly support. It flags two specific defects. First, the anachronism: star fort is a 16th-century European bastioned-artillery form and cannot be applied to circa 1100. Second, the electrical reading is simply unsupported. The entry is marked HELD-NULL and carries no source at all, with the operator's note that empty beats fabricated, and it recommends the event be reframed or retired.

What survives underneath is narrower and better attested. [E-W0-012-01] carries Cahokia at its peak around 1050 to 1150 as the largest urban centre north of the Mesoamerican cities, dominated by Monks Mound, with population estimates ranging between 6,000 and 40,000 — and it names the planned mound layout and solar alignments as the genuine documented phenomenon. That archaeology is held at tier B. The framework overlay on top of it, Cahokia as "American Levant governance" and as the Hardware side of the Managerial-Allodial split, is explicitly labelled the audit's interpretive layer at tier C rather than a claim of the archaeology.

The graph is worth looking at, because it is doing the work here. [E-W0-010-01] and [E-W0-009-01] both link to Cahokia and Cahokia links back to both, so the corpus has already assembled these three into a small cluster — and in a corpus organised around named threads, none of the three belongs to any thread. That is not an accident of tagging. The material the operator was willing to run through T-IBERIAN-RECONQUISTA-SOFTWARE or T-DISCOVERY-DOCTRINE is material he could source; this cluster was quarantined instead.

The third member shows why. [E-W0-009-01] corrects a conflation of the Maya Long Count with the roughly 26,000-year precessional cycle, noting the reached source makes no association between the two and that the framework's "Allodial Time" rests on precession, not on the Long Count. So you have three adjacent W0 entries, all touching pre-contact American astronomy and engineering, and all three are corrections of earlier overclaims. That is the same move three times in one neighbourhood.

And it is the same move the corpus makes elsewhere when a good story has no evidence. [E-W0-006-01] holds the 1311 Mali Atlantic crossing as HELD-NULL and says outright that a plausible current route is not evidence of a completed crossing. [E-W0-030-01] kills the Templar-founded-Swiss-banking claim on chronology, since the suppression of 1307 to 1314 postdates the 1291 charter. [E-W0-040-01] downgrades papal banking as "instrumental warrant" for Dum Diversas to structural adjacency, held rather than asserted. Your question lands on the one entry in that set most likely to be mistaken for a positive finding, because its title still reads as an assertion while its body is a withdrawal.
outside:
Two things the corpus does not spell out that make the retraction sharper.

The star fort anachronism is worse than a date problem. The bastioned trace, developed in Italy from the late fifteenth century, exists for a single reason: to angle walls so that gunpowder artillery cannot batter them flat and so that defenders can enfilade the ground in front of every face. Its geometry is a solution to a ballistics problem that did not exist anywhere in the world in 1100. Reading that shape backwards onto a mound complex imports the answer to a question nobody had yet asked.

The other is that "silicon substrate" quietly welds together two separate objects in this corpus. The silicon in [E-W0-011-01] is the Spruce Pine pegmatite district in western North Carolina, a product of the Alleghanian Orogeny — igneous and metamorphic rock in the Appalachians. Cahokia sits in the American Bottom, the Mississippi alluvial floodplain, hundreds of miles west, on unconsolidated river silt and clay. Whatever Monks Mound is built on, it is not the Spruce Pine formation. The two entries share a window and a framework vocabulary, not a geology, and the phrase in the title slides from one to the other without the corpus ever claiming they touch.

What is actually well documented at Cahokia and worth having instead: the Woodhenge post circles, the Grand Plaza as a deliberately engineered flat surface, the site's alignment on a north-south axis with solstice sightlines, and enormous coordinated earthmoving on a fixed plan. That is planning and astronomy at scale. It does not require electricity to be remarkable, and [E-W0-012-01] is where the corpus keeps it.

Additionally, the phrase "silicon substrate" silently conflates two unrelated objects: the Spruce Pine pegmatite district of western North Carolina (E-W0-011-01, Alleghanian Orogeny igneous/metamorphic rock) and Cahokia's setting in the American Bottom, unconsolidated Mississippi alluvial silt and clay hundreds of miles west. The two entries share a date window and framework vocabulary but no geology, and the retraction should say so.

The bastioned trace is a solution to a gunpowder-artillery ballistics problem (angled walls to resist battering, enfilade fire across every face) that did not exist anywhere in 1100, so the shape imports the answer to an unasked question. trigger_context: What year did the Transportation Act receive Royal Assent? One sentence.
raw_content: May 1717 — the Transportation Act (4 Geo 1 c 11) received Royal Assent that month, with the first Old Bailey transportation sentences following on 26 April 1718 [w3-1717-legal] [w3-1718-legal-april].
